newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Alberta to cut aviation fuel tax in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Alberta to cut aviation fuel tax in Jan.

text.p: The Canadian province of Alberta said on Monday that its aviation fuel tax was slated to drop to 1.5 cents (Canadian) from 5 cents per litre for domestic and international flights effective January 1, 1997.

A 2.5 cent per litre cut in the aviation fuel tax had been legislated to come into effect in 1998, but was accelerated in November as part of a rescue plan for financially troubled Canadian Airlines Corp.
The change in fuel tax rates applies to all carriers operating in Alberta and is part of Alberta's "reinvestment plan," announced in June, the provincial government said.
Alberta said the reduction would put aviation fuel prices well below those in all jurisdictions west of Canada's Maritime provinces.
The cost of the tax change to Alberta's budget was estimated at C$5.5 million for 1996-97 and C$22 million for 1997-98, the government said.
